labels.description: Adds recent U.S. federal and state government activities and proposals targeting drivers of childhood chronic disease, and a new demand risk from changes in funding for or restrictions on including the company's products in benefit programs such as SNAP.
labels.rationale: criterion 1 and 2: a new regulatory exposure is disclosed and a named program (SNAP) and new government initiatives are referenced.

labels.description: Adds affordability and consumer spending patterns and perceived undesirability of processed foods as drivers of shifting preferences, plus a new sentence that data analytics, automation and AI on digital platforms are reshaping how consumers discover and engage with brands.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new risk drivers (affordability, spending patterns, AI-driven changes in brand discovery) are disclosed.

labels.description: Extends failures to meet standards and past recalls to contract manufacturers, expands recall causes to misbranding, spoilage and undeclared allergens, drops the reference to value-added dairy and plant-based categories, and adds lost sales from production decreases during remediation and changes in consumer demand.
labels.rationale: criterion 1, 2 and 3: a new counterparty class and new recall causes are disclosed, named product categories are dropped, and the realized recall language is broadened.

labels.description: Only a page-number marker moved and a comma was removed before "or unintentional contaminants"; the text is otherwise identical.
labels.rationale: minor: punctuation and page-break placement only, no change in substance.

labels.description: "strong commitment to product safety and quality and human rights" becomes "strong commitment to product safety and quality and respecting human rights", and a page-number marker moved.
labels.rationale: minor: stylistic rewording with identical meaning plus page-break placement.

labels.description: The U.S. alcohol subsidiary's third-party arrangement changes from producing and selling in "certain regions of the United States" to producing, distributing and selling in "the United States".
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the scope of the disclosed alcohol business is widened from certain U.S. regions to the U.S. generally, with distribution added.

labels.description: Adds that for 2025 one bottler accounted for 10% of net operating revenues (EMEA and Asia Pacific segments, previously no concentration figure), and adds a new risk that bottlers' actions on quality, safety, labor, compliance or sustainability could harm brand value even when the company is not responsible.
labels.rationale: criterion 1 and 4: a new customer concentration figure (10% of revenue) and a new reputational exposure are disclosed.

labels.description: Only a page-number marker ("18") was inserted; the risk factor text is identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-break artifact only, no change in wording or substance.
